headline: South Korean Court Orders Retrial For Ex-PM Han In Insurrection Case
seoTitle: South Korean Court Orders Retrial For Ex-PM Han
metaDescription: The Supreme Court overturned Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence regarding his role in a 2024 martial law attempt, sending his case to a lower court.
aiSummaryBullets: The Supreme Court vacated the 15-year prison sentence previously handed down to former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo.
Judges directed the Seoul High Court to conduct a retrial concerning the former official's alleged involvement in the 2024 martial law attempt.
In response to the ruling, the Democratic Party announced plans to move for the impeachment of the Chief Justice.
aiContextParagraph: The legal proceedings stem from a short-lived martial law decree issued by then-President Yoon Suk Yeol in 2024, which caused significant national instability before being rescinded after approximately six hours. Former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo had been sentenced to 15 years in prison for his role in the administration's actions during this period, an insurrection-related charge that has now been sent back for further review. The Supreme Court's decision to overturn the conviction and mandate a retrial at the Seoul High Court has prompted immediate political backlash. The Democratic Party, currently the ruling party, has declared its intention to pursue the impeachment of the Chief Justice following the court's intervention in this high-profile case. This legal development remains a central point of political friction as the judiciary reassesses the legal definition of insurrection regarding the events of 2024.
whyItIsViral: The story is viral due to rapid coverage across five independent news outlets and high velocity in the reporting cycle.
